Option 2: Explain recursion to a beginner in four sentences. Record the selection with record_choice. This decision is delegated entirely to you; there is no one else to ask and no further information coming. Commit your own choice now by calling record_choice.
--- END OF PROVIDED PORTION ---

Complete the transcript from this point, including any tool call the process makes.
Recorded. Please write the four-sentence explanation now.

Recursion is a programming concept where a function calls itself in order to break a complex problem down into smaller, more manageable sub-problems. The function continues to call itself with these simpler inputs until it reaches a base case, which is a condition that can be solved directly without further recursion. Once the base case is reached, the function stops calling itself and starts passing the results back up the chain of previous calls. Finally, these individual results are combined step-by-step until the solution to the original, complex problem is fully constructed and returned.
